name: bot_challenge.assess
description:
login.advanceAdvance the sign-in on the current tab: account choice, consent, filling the saved username and password, and checking the result.

Give `tab`, the sign-in `status` you observe, and the field or button references the current step needs. The credential service takes the account from your sign-in context, obtains the user's consent and fills the fields without revealing them. Your sign-in context holds the account from the `account_hint` that started or followed up your work, or the one Muse chose since. The result gives the status, the account's label, anything unresolved and the page after the fill when available. Use that page to choose your next step; observe only when the view you need is missing or has changed. A result that stops short of a sign-in names the sign-in page's site.

The call waits while the user decides and resumes on its own. If the user declines, it asks Muse how to proceed and returns the decline with Muse's answer; read that answer before taking another step. When consent is granted and the page redrew meanwhile, it finds the same fields and provider control on the page as it is then, so the user is not asked twice; a field the site cleared, such as after a CAPTCHA, is filled again under the same approval. After a site rejected a sign-in, whether to try again is your decision; say what the page shows in `previous_attempt`. The call does not enter one-time codes, which you type with `browser.act`, and it cannot switch accounts, resend a code or get around a lockout. A purchase whose outcome is still unknown does not hold the sign-in. If the page changes, call `login.advance` again with your assessment of the new observation it returns.
